She stated this yesterday during the 2026 World Food Day celebration, organised by the Nigerian Association of Women in Agriculture (NAWIA), in Gusau, the state capital.
Mrs Lawal commended NAWIA for its contributions to agricultural development and the economic empowerment of women, describing the exhibition of farm produce and the participation of women farmers as evidence of its commitment to food security.
She also lauded the state coordinator of NAWIA, Hajiya Shema’u Mohammed Nalado, for her leadership and sustained efforts to empowering women and promoting agricultural development across the state.
The first lady also commended her husband, Governor Dauda Lawal, for supporting farmers through agricultural grants, fertiliser distribution and other interventions aimed at increasing food production.
She said farming remains an important part of Zamfara’s heritage and pledged that the government would continue to support farmers towards building a food-secure and prosperous state.
In her remarks, Hajiya Nalado, called on the federal and state governments, the Bank of Agriculture and development partners to provide women farmers with accessible loans, modern farm inputs and training.
She said women remain central to food security and agricultural development despite challenges such as insecurity, inadequate financing, limited access to modern farm equipment and climate change.
Nalado disclosed that NAWIA has over 3,000 women engaged in various agricultural activities across the state, including rice, millet, groundnut, poultry and vegetable production.
She said the association had recently received accreditation to provide skills training for more women and youths, a development she said would expand opportunities in agricultural production and improve livelihoods.
The World Food Day celebration featured an exhibition of farm produce by farmers from various local government areas of the state.
